title: John and Lawrence Marrero
summary: Sayles praises John Marrero as a fine banjoist who composed and left for New York, and remembers Lawrence Marrero in a Tuxedo band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Uh, go back to the, uh, going back to the early days a bit, uh, what can you remember about John Marrero, you know? What kind of stuff you remember?

Well, John Marrero was a fine banjo player. I remember him when he played with, uh, the Bay Rizley band, which Celestine was the trumpet player. Mm-hmm. Emma Barrett was the piano player. Uh, uh, Simon was the bass player. And, uh, uh, Paul Barberin was the clarinet and saxophone player. And, uh, I mean, yeah, Chani Fawcett, Abbie Fawcett was on drums, yeah. Oh, yeah. I remember he was a very fine banjo player. Mm-hmm.
Did, uh, were they, you know, you heard the records that he made, uh, John Marrero. Are they good examples of his playing, or did he play four or four most of the time?
Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah. He had a very, in fact, he was one of the best banjo players we had, Ryan. Yeah.
Cause he did a lot of composing, too, didn't he?
Yeah, I heard he wrote a lot of numbers. He wrote some, uh, swing numbers and jazz numbers, and he wrote some nice ballads. Yeah.
He was going, I guess, when you were coming up, was he? Or?

Oh, no, no. He was, he was, uh, when the last time I saw John, he was working at the La Vida Club, I tell you, when I, when John's calling them. Oh, yeah. I was the one who took his place when he went to New York. Yeah?
Mm-hmm.
Oh, he went to New York. Yeah, that's the last time I saw him, and the next thing I heard, he had died. I don't remember what year, as a present, he died.
Uh, how about his brother Lawrence? What do you know?
Well, Lawrence was, was playing around there. stuff
I don't remember what you wear. Lawrence was playing with a band I used to call the Second Tuxedo Band.
Young Tuxedo?
Young Tuxedo, something like that, yeah. I remember the piano player was named Dwight Newman. His son is the terrific trumpet player we have today, Joe Newman, yeah.
And Lawrence would play a straight 4-4 even.
Yeah, he was mostly a straight 4-4 band. But he wasn't, to me, a good solo like John was.
No, no, no. You remember who taught John Marrero, do you know?
No, I don't. I don't remember that. I know the whole family, but I don't remember who taught him.
Remember who taught Lawrence?
Well, maybe...
John?
I think John was playing before Lawrence, I think. Oh, yeah, yeah. Yeah.
